# Purpose and Applicability {#PurposeSection}

These guidelines describe the minimum data standards and recommended practices for reporting data collected under the IOTC Regional Observer Scheme (ROS) by onboard observers and through Electronic Monitoring Systems (EMS). They aim to promote the consistency, completeness and quality of ROS data submitted to the Secretariat of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC).

The guidelines are intended as a reference for [IOTC Contracting Parties and Cooperating Non-Contracting Parties](https://iotc.org/about-iotc/structure-commission) (CPCs) when preparing and submitting ROS data to the IOTC Secretariat. They describe the ROS reporting forms, data standards and submission procedures, including requirements that differ according to fishing gear, data source or species group.

The guidelines apply to data reported under the ROS for vessels subject to the requirements of the Scheme, including vessels of 24 metres length overall and above, and vessels under 24 metres length overall when operating outside their exclusive economic zone (EEZ). They cover data derived from onboard observation and, where applicable, EMS.

These guidelines should be used together with the applicable [IOTC ROS Standards](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/ROS/Standards/IOTC_Regional_Observer_Scheme_Standards.pdf), [ROS EMS Programme Standards](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/ROS/Standards/Electronic_monitoring_program_standards.pdf), and current [IOTC Conservation and Management Measures](https://iotc.org/cmms) (CMMs). As reporting requirements may evolve, the provisions of the applicable CMMs shall prevail in the event of any inconsistency.
